newsitem.title: USA: Salt River expects to end transmission dispute Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Salt River expects to end transmission dispute Wednesday.

text.p: The Salt River Project (SRP) expects to resolve by late Wednesday a dispute over access to El Paso Electric Co transmission lines into Mexico, SRP said Tuesday.

SRP, a public power utility based in Phoenix, Arizona, was the low bidder for a contract to supply Mexico's national utility, Comision Federal de Electricidad (CFE), with 200 megawatts during calendar 1997.
But El Paso, which currently supplies CFE with the power, maintains it does not have enough extra transmission capacity to carry power from Arizona and further into Mexico.
The west Texas-based utility has filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to protest SRP's claim of open access to transmission.
Lisa Urias, head of SRP's Mexican power group, said Tuesday "we are fighting pretty hard. It remains to be seen whether we will strike a deal or whether we will have to file with FERC."
Both SRP and CFE would prefer to avoid a drawn out FERC proceeding, and SRP has offered to share a portion of the Mexican contract with El Paso, she said.
"They (El Paso) want to be made whole and we have done everything we can to accomdate them. But El Paso would like to keep their monopoly," Urias said.
She said previously that SRP's bid was substantially under CFE's current price from El Paso of $45.00 per megawatt hour.
CFE had allowed SRP 10 days to finalize transmission details, but that deadline has been extended to Thursday, SRP said.
